rows.question: Q1a
rows.rubricFeedback: Full marks: identified {rollNo} and {email} as the candidate keys and explained why {rollNo, hostel} is only a superkey.

rows.question: Q1b
rows.rubricFeedback: Mapped every entity and relationship correctly but drew the foreign-key arrow from Enrolment to Course without naming the referencing attribute courseId.

rows.question: Q2a
rows.rubricFeedback: Wrote a correct expression but did not show the relation it produces on the sample instance, which the question asked for.

rows.question: Q2b
rows.rubricFeedback: Full marks: pushed σ dept = 'CS' below the Student ⋈ Enrolment join and justified it by the predicate using only Student's attributes.

rows.question: Q3a
rows.rubricFeedback: Full marks: derived A → D in two justified transitivity steps, A → C from A → B and B → C, then A → D from C → D.

rows.question: Q3b
rows.rubricFeedback: Wrote {B}+ = {B, C}, missing D because C → D was never applied after B → C had added C.

rows.question: Q3c
rows.rubricFeedback: Full marks: listed AE, BE, CE and DE as the candidate keys and noted that E is in every key because no dependency derives it.

rows.question: Q1a
rows.rubricFeedback: Full marks: gave the timer interrupt for Running → Ready, an I/O request for Running → Waiting and process exit for Running → Terminated.

rows.question: Q1b
rows.rubricFeedback: Drew every state and arc of the five-state model but left the admit and exit arcs unlabelled, losing the mark for naming each transition.

rows.question: Q2a
rows.rubricFeedback: Full marks: separated per-thread state (stack, registers, program counter) from process-wide state (heap, globals, open files).

rows.question: Q2b
rows.rubricFeedback: Said a blocking read stalls the whole process without stating that this holds only for the many-to-one threading model, which the question left open.

rows.question: Q3a
rows.rubricFeedback: Full marks: saved state to the outgoing PCB, ran the scheduler, restored the incoming PCB and noted that a system call alone is only a mode switch.

rows.question: Q3b
rows.rubricFeedback: Full marks: computed the switching overhead as 0.5 / (10 + 0.5), about 4.8 percent of CPU time.

rows.question: Q3c
rows.rubricFeedback: Stated that halving the quantum roughly doubles the overhead but gave no 0.5 / 5.5 calculation to support it, so the method mark was withheld.
